```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE,
                      collapse = TRUE,
                        comment = "#>")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.align = "center")
```

Below, you can find examples on how to use some of the core functions of the hibiiscus package.

* First, we show how to create a hibiiscus database (based on data from the 
PREDICTS project, see <https://www.nhm.ac.uk/our-science/our-work/biodiversity/predicts.html>).

* We then show various ways in which a hibiiscus database object can be manipulated,
for example filtering to remove particular sites, or realigning land-use variables.
We follow this by saving the hibiiscus database for future use.

* Next, diversity metrics for each site will be calculated, before fitting a mixed-effects
model using `lme4`.

* We then demonstrate the use of cross-validation to interogate model performance.

* Before finishing with an example of model projection.


### 1. Load package and PREDICTS-like data

```{r Load packages}
# library(hibiiscus)
devtools::load_all()

```

```{r Load data, cache=F, warning=FALSE}
# PREDICTS data, 2016 release
hib_db <- create_hib(path_species = "~/Documents/IIASA/lamasus/raw_data/PREDICTS/2016/database.rds", 
                     path_sites   = "~/Documents/IIASA/lamasus/raw_data/PREDICTS/2016/sites.rds", 
                     version = "2016")

# View a summary of the hib database object
print(hib_db)

```


### 2. Filter data to focus on European sites and remove locations where land-use is unclear

```{r Filter data, cache=F}
hib_db <- hib_filter_sites(hib_db, 
                           UN_region == "Europe" &
                             Predominant_land_use != "Cannot decide")
```

```{r Simple plot of data, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
hib_db$plot()
```

### 3. Condense land-use categories 
Here, we will add a new column to the site data, effectively grouping land-use types into
"Natural", "Semi-natural" and "Human".

```{r Group LU types, cache=F}
alt_lu_df <- data.frame("Predominant_land_use"= c("Primary vegetation",
                                                  "Mature secondary vegetation",
                                                  "Intermediate secondary vegetation",
                                                  "Young secondary vegetation",
                                                  "Secondary vegetation (indeterminate age)",
                                                  "Plantation forest",
                                                  "Pasture",
                                                  "Cropland",
                                                  "Urban"),
                        "Grouped_LU" = c("Natural", "Natural", 
                                         "Semi-natural",  "Semi-natural", "Semi-natural",
                                         "Human", "Human", "Human", "Human"))

alt_lu_df$Grouped_LU <- factor(alt_lu_df$Grouped_LU,
                               levels = c("Natural", "Semi-natural", "Human"))
hib_db <- hib_join_sites(hib_db,
                         alt_lu_df)


# Save the database object for future use
# save_hib(hib_db, 
#          "../Data/example_hib.rds")

```


### 4. Correct measurements for sampling effort and calculate total abundance per site

```{r Diversity metrics, cache=F}
hib_db$hib_effort_correction()

# hib_db <- hib_calc_ta(hib_db)
hib_db <- hib_calc_div_within(hib_db,
                              c("Total_abundance"))

print(hib_db)

```
Note: other metrics of within-site diversity include; "Species_richness", "Chao1_diversity", "Simpson_diversity", "Shannon_diversity", "Mean_abundance", "Geometric_mean_abundance", "HillShannon_diversity", "HillSimpson_diversity" and "PIE".


### 5. Fit a simple model of total abundance in response to land-use

```{r Fit model, cache=F}
hib_ta_mod <- hib_fit_lme4(hib_db,
                           sqrt(Rescaled_total_abundance) ~ Grouped_LU + (1 | SS) + (1 | SSB),
                           REML = F,
                           calc_CIs = "Wald")

print(hib_ta_mod)

```

```{r Simple plot of fixed-effect coefficients, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
hib_ta_mod$plot()
```

```{r Simple plot of random-effect coefficients, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
hib_ta_mod$plot("random-effects")
```


### 6. Cross-validate the fitted model, using both Random, and geographically blocked folds.

```{r Cross-validate model, cache=F}
# Cross-validate model, include a back-transformation to obtain predictions/errors
# on the scale of Rescaled_total_abundance
hib_cv <- hib_mod_cv(hib_ta_mod,
                     hib_db,
                     fold_type = c("Random-5", "Biome"),
                     backtransform = function(x){x^2})

print(hib_cv)

```

Note: other cross-validation approaches include; "Random-2", "Random-3", "Random-5", "Random-10", "Source_ID", "SS", "Country", "UN_subregion", "UN_region", "Biome", "Realm" and "Custom". 
When using "Custom", any grouping variable can be specified, as long as it is present in the site data.


```{r Simple plot of cross-validation folds, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
hib_cv$plot("map-sites")
```

```{r Simple plot of variation in fixed-effects coefficients, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
hib_cv$plot("coefficients")
```

```{r Simple plot of model performance, fig.width=6, fig.height=5, warning=F}
hib_cv$plot("metrics",
            c("corsq", "mae", "rmse", "rsq"))
```

Note: In the above figures displaying coefficients and predictive performance, the black line and grey shading indicate the values and confidence intervals, respectively, estimated based on a model fitted to the complete dataset (In-sample).


### 7. Model projection

```{r Generate an example 10x10 df for use in projection}
# Generate a simple df of example land-uses for projection.
proj_df <- expand.grid(x = 1:10,
            y = 1:10) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Forest_cover = runif(dplyr::n()),
                Grouped_LU = dplyr::case_when(Forest_cover <= 0.3 ~ "Human",
                                              Forest_cover > 0.3 & Forest_cover <= 0.7 ~ "Semi-natural",
                                              Forest_cover > 0.7 ~ "Natural",
                                              T ~ NA))
```

```{r Project the model}
hib_proj <- hib_mod_project(hib_ta_mod,
                proj_df, 
                backtransform = function(x){x^2},
                rescale_pred = T,
                lme4_boot = T, n_boot = 50)
```

```{r Simple plot of projection, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
hib_proj$plot(response_var = "rescaled_prediction_mean")
```

```{r Bivariate map of projected values and uncertainty, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=5}
hib_proj$plot("bivariate-map")
```

```{r Simple plot of distribution of projected values, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
hib_proj$plot("response-distr", response_var = "rescaled_prediction_mean")
```
